# Every netlink.LinkAdd in pkg/ and the parent-interface gate that
# covers it (#571).
#
# WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR
#
# A parent NIC registers one rx_handler, so it is a macvlan port or an
# ipvlan port and never both. Any child link attached to a parent must
# therefore be serialised against every other operation on that parent,
# which is what Plugin.lockParent does. A LinkAdd that reaches a parent
# without holding that gate can be refused with "device or resource
# busy" — surfacing to a user as a failed `docker run` caused by an
# unrelated container.
#
# HOW THIS FILE AND THE COMPILER DIVIDE THE WORK
#
# Most of the gate is proved by the type system, not here. lockParent
# returns a *parentGuard and addChildLink takes one, so a child link
# created through addChildLink is holding the gate as a matter of
# compilation, at every site, however many frames separate the lock
# from the LinkAdd.
#
# That leaves TWO ways round it, and the script covers both.
#
# 1. Call netlink.LinkAdd directly and skip the helper. This file is
#    the check on that path: the script matches every netlink.LinkAdd
#    in pkg/ — the SUPERSET, however it is gated — and fails when a
#    file is unlisted, when a count has changed, or when an entry has
#    no justification. The bypass stays possible, because bridge
#    networks legitimately need it; what stops is it happening without
#    anyone deciding it.
#
# 2. Forge a guard. parentGuard's zero value is valid Go, so
#    `addChildLink(&parentGuard{}, link)` compiles and holds nothing.
#    "Only lockParent constructs one" is not a thing the type system
#    can say, so the script fails the build on a parentGuard built
#    anywhere but parent_gate.go.
#
# So: the compiler answers "is a guard present at the LinkAdd", and
# this script answers "is the guard real, and is anything off the
# guarded path". Neither question is answered by the other, which is
# why both exist — and why the compiler half must not be described as
# doing all of it.
#
# FORMAT
#
#   <path> <count>
#       <justification, indented, one or more lines>
#
# Entries are separated by blank lines. A bare path with no
# justification fails the gate: a list of paths with no reasons becomes
# a list somebody appends to. Same rule as .github/vuln-allowlist.txt.

pkg/plugin/parent_gate.go 1
    THE funnel. This is addChildLink, and it is the only place in the
    plugin that attaches a child link to a parent NIC. It takes a
    *parentGuard it never reads: the parameter exists so the caller
    cannot reach this line without having gone through lockParent, which
    is what makes the requirement a compile error rather than a review
    comment.
    Every parent-attached site in the plugin — the endpoint's own child
    in parent_attached.go, the validate_dhcp preflight probe in
    dhcp_probe.go — reaches the kernel through here.
    A third site used to sit here: the orphaned-lease reclaim's
    temporary link in orphan_release.go. That whole mechanism was
    removed in v1.9.0 (#800) because it raced the tombstone that
    promises a restarting container its address back. Its entry in this
    file went with it. The gate itself did NOT become unnecessary — the
    probe still holds a parent across a DHCP round trip.

pkg/plugin/network.go 1
    The bridge-mode veth pair created at CreateEndpoint. Same reasoning
    as the bridge branch above: no parent NIC, nothing to serialise
    against, and adding a gate here would serialise bridge endpoints
    against nothing.
